candidates.title: Voice Relay to a Working Agent
candidates.summary: A realtime voice call with a front-line voice agent that hands work to the coding agent, answers questions about its progress and speaks short updates while it runs.
candidates.behavior: With the agent idle and the input empty, the Send slot becomes a waveform "Start voice chat" button. The person describes a change out loud; the voice agent hands it to the chat's coding agent. They keep talking while it runs, asking what changed in a diff or how a run is going, and hear short progress notes and a brief spoken summary on completion instead of the full written reply. The call can be muted or ended from outside the app (iOS Lock Screen Live Activity).

criteria.aiSpecific: (a) Spoken oversight of a long-running agent: the person needs a way to delegate and follow work without reading output.
criteria.distinct: (c) Voice Orb/Listening State/Live Transcript cover the conversation itself; here the voice agent is a relay with state about another agent's run, speaks progress and summarises results.

candidates.difference: Voice is a control and status channel for a separate task-running agent, not the conversation with the model that does the work.

evidence.quote: Describe a change out loud, ask what an agent is working on, and hear updates as the work moves forward.

candidates.title: Publish Gate
candidates.summary: Before an agent-built app goes live, automated and agent-based security checks run; failures go back to the agent to fix, and nothing is published until the person explicitly confirms.
candidates.behavior: The person picks a domain and chooses to publish. Cursor runs deterministic rules plus agent review for issues such as exposed secrets. If a check fails, the agent says what it needs to fix. Only when checks pass can the person explicitly publish; admins can approve a blocked publish, add review rules and unpublish any app. Sharing is then scoped to people, groups or the team.

criteria.aiSpecific: (a) Agents generate and ship code the person has not read, so a checkpoint must catch leaked secrets before release.
criteria.observed: (b) Cursor changelog, 2026-11-05. GitHub Copilot Agent Merge, 2026-11-06.
criteria.distinct: (c) Tool Approval gates individual actions and Diff Summary reviews code changes; this gates release of the whole artifact on a pass/fail check with admin override.

candidates.difference: A release-time gate combining automated checks, agent remediation and explicit confirmation.

evidence.quote: Nothing goes live until the checks pass and you explicitly publish the app.
Set up Agent Merge directly from a pull request to have Copilot merge it when it’s ready. It now stays enabled while required checks or rules are pending.

candidates.title: Rejected Prompt Restore
candidates.summary: When an agent refuses the first prompt of a session, the prompt goes back into the composer with the reason shown, so the person can fix it and resend without retyping.
candidates.behavior: The person sends the opening prompt of a local agent session. If the agent rejects it, no empty or failed session is left behind: the text reappears in the composer, the rejection reason is shown with it, and the person edits and resends.

criteria.aiSpecific: (a) An agent can decline a request for policy or capability reasons; the person needs to know why and keep their words.
criteria.distinct: (c) Generation Error and Chat Bubble retry a failed reply; here the input itself is returned for editing, with the agent's reason, before a session exists.

candidates.difference: Recovery keeps the person's prompt and puts it back where they can change it, instead of showing an error after it.

evidence.quote: If a local agent rejects the first prompt, Desktop puts the text back in the composer and shows the reason. You can correct it and resend without retyping.
